planting.note: Plant fleshy root divisions 3-4 inches deep in moist, humus-rich soil with sharp drainage in partial shade; this hybrid emerges later than most perennials in spring, so mark the spot to avoid digging into dormant roots.

directions: Plant fleshy root divisions 3-4 inches deep in moist, humus-rich soil with sharp winter drainage, siting in dappled shade sheltered from drying wind. 'Harvington Raw Silk' is a UK-bred hybrid between Roscoea cautleyoides and Roscoea humeana selected for unusually large, pale cream-to-soft-yellow orchid-like flowers that open from red-flushed buds held just above narrow, upright, strap-shaped foliage in early summer. It has earned the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its vigor, free flowering, and tolerance of average garden conditions compared to fussier roscoea species, and benefits from a mulch in winter to protect the storage roots from hard freezes. Pair with hostas, hardy ferns, and other woodland-edge perennials in a lightly shaded border or large container that can be kept dry when dormant.

directions: Plant fleshy root divisions 3-4 inches deep in consistently moist, humus-rich soil with good winter drainage, in dappled shade protected from harsh midday sun. 'Harvington Evening Star' is a vigorous, clump-forming Roscoea hybrid bred by UK nurseryman Hugh Nunn, prized for flowers of an unusually deep purple-black shade freshly opened, each marked with a small cluster of white flecks at the throat that appear to twinkle against the dark petals. Blooms are carried on compact, upright stems above narrow, ginger-like foliage from early to midsummer, and established clumps multiply steadily without becoming invasive.
